Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished landscape individual concept sheet for an additional SECOND STAGE design choice in Festival Tycoon. Reference 1 is approved crafted low-poly English rural festival art direction. Reference 2 is actual existing trailer-stage scale in game, for small performer/attendee scale only, not UI. This new stage must feel more intentional and purpose-built than a farm trailer, but still low-fi inexpensive small countryside festival. NO roof, canopy, cover, overhead beams, tall truss, tall backdrop, huge banners, lighting tower, mosaic surface, wheels or trailer hitch. Open performance deck visible from all four isometric camera directions. Any rear/side treatment low and sparse, no solid performer-height walls. No invented capacity, price, tier, unlock or stats.
Sheet layout: cream paper, forest-green headings, main front three-quarter hero about 65% area, two small secondary views at right (rear three-quarter EMPTY deck and side elevation), one plain adult attendee standing beside front corner as scale cue. Same small removable drum kit, microphone and two modest black speakers in hero only, not built into deck. Keep props sparse. One simple deck/support connection detail inset. Rear/side views must depict same geometry consistently. Low-poly faceted original geometry with broad matte materials, few wood-grain cues rather than photoreal microtexture. Rural grass patch only, no venue redesign. Label secondary panels "REAR / OPEN DECK", "SIDE / SCALE", "CONSTRUCTION CUE". Footer "CONCEPT ONLY — additional stage choice". Include small note "Instruments and speakers shown for scale; removable." Clear readable short typography. No mechanical build, no guarantee of runtime sightline verification.
Design A: "A / TIMBER DAIS". Subtitle "Low, open and deliberately built". Distinctive shallow chamfered-front polygonal timber deck, honey/sage natural timber on stout short exposed square wooden posts and simple crossbeams. Broad integrated two-level front step/apron follows front chamfered silhouette, inviting village-event dais rather than the existing high rectangular railed stage. Keep platform roughly adult knee height, wide enough for a small band; person height consistent with approx 4 adult heights across width. Entire rear edge open, only tiny corner stops below knee if needed. No wraparound rail enclosure, no black steel structure. Timber carpentry is tidy but simple and scuffed. Modelling cue text "Chamfered deck / broad step / short timber posts". Hero clear top of deck, open leg spaces, grounded feet.

Design B: "B / FARMYARD PLATFORM". Subtitle "Reclaimed boards, solid rural character". Genuinely distinct from an elevated timber dais: broad shallow RECTANGULAR loading-dock-like stage, low adult-knee-height, supported on squat reclaimed brick/stone piers, dark reused sleeper perimeter beams, a mostly closed weathered vertical-board FRONT fascia with small service gap at rear. Honest broad varied grey-brown and faded sage planks, deliberate stable flush performance floor, not pallet gaps or loose hay. A compact SIDE stair tucked onto right end, no wide front step. A sparse short string of small faded triangular bunting attached directly across front fascia BELOW deck height, never above heads. The low solid base and asymmetrical side entry make this structurally and visually different. No rail enclosure, high poles, hay-bale floor, masonry walls above deck or canopy. Small pale masonry feet visible at corners. Modelling cue text "Sleeper frame / reclaimed fascia / masonry piers". Warm handmade farmyard character without clutter.

Design C: "C / MODULAR RISER". Subtitle "Practical hire-kit, assembled for the field". A compact rectangular slightly taller platform around adult mid-thigh height with visibly repeating dark charcoal plywood DECK PANELS in a simple 3 by 2 grid, slim dull galvanised steel edge frames, tubular vertical legs and restrained diagonal bracing entirely BELOW deck, small flat ground pads. A detachable narrow metal stair at left end with short handrail that ends at deck height. TWO short low tubular rear-corner guard sections only, widely open centre, no enclosing cage, no high truss. Industrial modest hire-kit look, matte worn grey steel and charcoal deck with small warm wood panel edge accents; not a polished concert stage. This must look physically different from wooden solid-fascia/platform directions. No cloth skirt, no overhead equipment, no wheels. Modelling cue text "Repeatable deck panels / steel legs / detachable stair". Clearly readable open underside.
